mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising month-over-month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance with persistent inflation, which typically precedes equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 200,000 new jobs per month for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month change > 200,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a deepening consumer demand slump, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
